candidates: The tagDeviceUI function adds the device to the local cache (line 87) before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice (line 93). When ErrDeviceLimitReached is returned because the device limit is reached and the device doesn't exist, the cache entry remains. On the next request, the cache hit at line 83-84 causes an early return with no error, bypassing the database check entirely. This allows blocked devices to authenticate successfully on retry within the 29-minute cache TTL, defeating the device limit feature.

The constant 30 * 24 * time.Hour representing the anonymous device expiration period is now defined in three separate files: anonymousDeviceExpiration in database.go, anonymousDeviceExpiration in api/api.go, and thirtyDays in impl.go. This PR adds a new duplicate in database.go instead of consolidating into a single exported constant. If the expiration period ever changes, it would need to be updated in multiple places, increasing maintenance burden and risk of inconsistency.
